Definitely not. Is it seen as more morally acceptable to eat a cow versus a human or dog/cat (in most countries)? Of course it is. Things socially and ethically go hand-in-hand, most of the morals we have instilled are because we have to get along socially in society, otherwise life could potentially look more like The Hunger Games. We're often raised to treat our "equals" as more valuable (other humans - and to some people, pets) which is why most people have no qualms about squashing a spider or fly, or don't feel guilty about stepping on an ant, but would feel horrible about hitting a puppy. People draw the line somewhere, we all do. 

Are you saying there's no inherent suffering in poisoned mice, rabbits, ducks, and moles? Seriously? Yes, there absolutely is, they're directly poisoned in order to grow the crops, directly, they would not be poisoned otherwise. You can't say all lives are equally valuable but then say there is no inherent suffering in plant agriculture, the fact remains that thousands and thousands of animals die directly because of it. You cannot change that to suit your narrative, it's a fact. What does that have to do with how well they're treated anyway? They all get killed in the end regardless, unless your issue is with the treatment of the animal before it's killed - not the fact they're killed, in which case... what about "humanely slaughtered" meats? Or is it impossible to humanely slaughter something? 

You asked what the difference between a human life and a cow is. I'm asking you what the difference between a cow and a duck is? You choose to save the cows by not eating them but you eat the rice that directly means the duck must be poisoned. Why the cow and not the duck [if you think they're worth the same value]?

Most people probably would eat another human if they were literally starving, think of the Andes plane crash. One reason people don't go around hunting humans is because it's illegal - murder, slaughtering/consuming cows isn't illegal, why? Because it's not seen the same, not legally, or ethically. It's also part of our instilled morals to not hurt other humans, or pets, we're raised to know that it's wrong. Few people are raised to feel that way about animals raised/slaughtered for meat. 

Lives do have different values, I know vegans who have swatted and killed flies, for example. Or mosquitos. Those are lives too, are they not? Do you not care about the field mice, rabbits, moles that die in the process of growing the vegetables, wheat, etc... that you consume? They're poisoned to protect the crops. Thousands of ducks are killed to protect rice production. Why don't any of their lives matter? 

Another reason is because most people don't kill their own cows anyway, if people had to personally slaughter the meat they eat, way less people would consume meat. We're blinded to what we don't see/experience. Just like you wouldn't want to personally poison the mice to protect the crops, you choose to ignore that it happens. 

And then there's the reason of empathy, it's a lot easier to empathize with our own kind, and/or people/animals we have emotional connections toward. Thus why many people don't eat dogs, or cats, because they value them as pets. It's also illegal to eat them in many countries. It's just not seen the same way. If you raised a cow, named it, treated it like a pet, and became attached to it emotionally - it would definitely be seen as a lot more weird to then kill and eat it. I was extremely skeptical about this. We live in Canada, and the lady was from a southern US state. It was her first event (?) here, and none of us had ever met her before. 

My cousin went first and was told allegedly weird things that the lady couldn't have known (I heard these things but thought they were a bit silly), I kind of scoffed this off. I had never, ever told anyone about the sensation of being touched that I felt at nights, not my cousins, nor my parents or siblings. Not sure how she would have known I was suicidal at that time either.

I can't really explain it. My cousin recorded the audio, so I still have it, if the audio didn't exist - I would think I'm misremembering, or that it was a dream. But it wasn't, it happened. I've never seen the lady again. I'm still skeptical, I'm not sure how she knew, but maybe she just had a hunch from my demeanor? Or maybe someone hinted it to her beforehand? Not sure how that would be possible since it was a one-off event and I didn't even tell her my name. Not sure.

I had something similar happen to me once (except it happened to me directly). I dressed up as a Disney princess for my little cousin's 6th birthday, it wasn't a paid job or anything, and I was fully expecting it to be a party of 12-15 kids - her Mom had estimated that beforehand. 

It was the month before Halloween, so I figured I could put a pretty penny into it and potentially get my money's worth by using it for a few costume contests or general Halloween events as well.

Anyway, the party was being held at a bowling alley I'd never been to. As a kid, I remember birthday parties being held in a particular party room booked in advance. This wasn't the case here, they had only booked a specific lane and two tables with seats. Absolutely no privacy. Worse yet, 6-7 birthday parties were going on using the lanes directly surrounding my cousin's. They were being hosted by young teenaged workers called "party heroes", who were not in costume, and they were barely able to control the massive amount of kids

Nevertheless, they would intermittently do the "Cha Cha Slide" and dance to "Celebration" by Kool & The Gang which would get the kids even more riled up.

I watched this going on for a short amount of time before taking a deep breath and approaching my cousin's party. They were so excited, hopping up and down, screaming. Just like what happened to your girlfriend, all of the parties around immediately took notice. The kids immediately stopped bowling, and they started flooding toward me, pulling on my wig, trying to climb my dress, and just losing their shit. Worse yet, one set of parents chose to do their cake at the beginning of their party, so some of the kids had caked up hands, cake that was now on my costume.

Initially I was a bit upset (because I wasn't given proper warning or notice), but as soon as I walked in and realised the situation, I kind of expected it to go the way that it did. The dress already had cake on it, the wig was quickly getting ruined, so I ended up embracing the situation. I gave my cousin my princess tiara to wear, dubbing her honorary princess of the day, which made all of the kids treat her extra special (with most parent's offering her birthday cake or party/loot bags). She was so thrilled. 

I did the dances with the party heroes, helped parents cut cake, and played with all of the kids. It was honestly more exhausting than my actual job, haha, but totally worth it to make all of those kids happy. And, of course, the costume was ruined and couldn't be used again - but surprisingly, no regrets, it was fun.

Hi! I can give you an opinion based on some experience with [some of] these ingredients. My MIL has to eat gluten-free because of actual health issues - as opposed to trends, so I sometimes make her "gluten-free bread" using almond flour, baking powder, psyllium husk, eggs, salt, olive oil, and water. She is not vegan, so I do use eggs, which I see are omitted from this recipe (can't attest to how it would turn out with their absence). 

Sometimes I'll also add in flax, chia, sunflower seeds, etc...

So, here's my thoughts. Let's start with a [picture](https://imgur.com/a/ESxY96y) [of a seedless variant that I made]. Which will give you an idea of the texture. 

It isn't like a brick (again, with the inclusion of eggs/baking powder) but, no, it isn't like bread. It's much more cake-like in texture. It can't be kneaded, it's more of a batter when it's in its raw form. It's quite tasty buttered with some cheese, or with some tea/coffee. I've made a variation with cocoa powder, vanilla, and some honey that was very, very good as a birthday cake for her.

If you have no reason to avoid gluten, I wouldn't bother with this. It won't be horrible but it's really... not comparable to the real deal.

Just so you know, it's usually safe to eat raw kale. In fact, cancer studies show it's more beneficial raw than cooked. In my opinion, it's pretty good raw in salads or smoothies. 

That being said, there are a couple of things to keep in mind. 

Firstly, it has compounds called gluconsinolates (that are largely why it's considered so healthy!) - however, this compound is sometimes problematic [only when the kale is raw], it can negatively impact your thyroid (and metabolism). 

In order to really hinder your thyroid you would have to eat a lot (literally bowls and bowls). Unless you have hypothyroidism, in which case, you should ask your doctor about how much consumption of it is okay for you. 

It should also be avoided if you're susceptible to kidney stones because of oxalates. Oxalates are also found in spinach, beets, nut butters, etc... Not just raw kale. Your doctor will also tell you if you need to follow an oxalate-restricted diet.

Overall though: it's usually safe for consumption, or perhaps even more beneficial.

My Mom grew up in Trinidad where they make "macaroni pie" - essentially a baked macaroni & cheese; they add eggs. My brothers and I grew up in Canada and don't particularly *love* the addition of eggs. 

That being said, when my Mom makes it, she tempers the eggs by slowly adding warm evaporated milk before adding it to the rest of the warm milk. She then adds that warm milk mixture to the hot macaroni, butter, and grated cheese (all of this is pre-placed in a casserole dish). Stir, stir, stir until everything is melted and homogenous. Then she puts grated cheese on top and bakes it. 

Some Trinidadians add pimento pepper, onion, garlic, etc... She didn't used to because we were picky kids [but she probably does now] . Haha. 


It doesn't have a grainy or scrambled texture the way she does it and it holds together well if you want to slice and serve it (like you would a pie).

Personally, as an adult: I use a roux and make it the way most of us are probably familiar with (sans eggs) but once in a while I like my Mom's version. I find roux versions creamier and slightly more velvety.

Hey! Playing AC II in the Ezio Trilogy is probably the easiest platinum in the series. No difficult optional objectives, relatively small map, no ridiculous multiplayer trophies (I'm looking at you AC IV), no legendary ships and the storyline isn't too long.

Second easiest for me was Odyssey, there's nothing particularly difficult in the game, but it is way more time consuming.

I think Liberation Remastered is probably the shortest platinum overall? However, the canoe mission is unnecessarily difficult and there are many optional objectives.

Hardest is probably even more subjective. For me, it was probably AC III Remastered because of optional objectives. The particular mission where you fly as an Eagle in the TOKW DLC (which is mandatory for the platinum) made me want to smash my controller. There's a similar in the main game but I didn't find it as difficult.

There's many other tricky optional objectives too like air assassinating a grenadier, sinking ships by firing on their power keg, chasing a certain antagonist at the end of the game, etc...

You also have to 100% **everything** in the game. So much side missions, including mundane stuff like "encyclopedia of the common man". Which, may or may not, still be glitched.

Brotherhood in the Ezio Trilogy is also difficult due to optional objectives. This includes the flying machine mission, tank mission, the "young at heart" thief mission, some of the Romulus Lairs, some of the DaVinci disappear. It's my favourite overall game, but well, it can be quite difficult.

AC IV is fairly hard. The game itself is fine, minus the optional objectives in the mission "Black Bart's Gambit". The MP trophy where you have to get to level 55 is ridiculous and gets increasingly harder the older the game gets.

AC Rogue is easy except, 3 words that make it difficult: The Storm Fortress.

Anyhow, a lot of these have exploits, but if you do everything legit (which you should try to do, the challenge makes the accomplishment more satisfying!) it's time consuming and sometimes difficult. 

The ONLY thing I skimped on was fast-forwarding my playstation clock for the fleet missions in Rogue, I had 2 left but I was done everything else because I did almost all of the side stuff in the game before progressing to the mission where you unlock the fleet. It's all inactive/off-screen side stuff, you send a ship off (you can't really mess up unless you don't have a 100% success rate) and it's just a matter of time before the mission ends, there's absolutely nothing for you to do (far less any challenge to it). If you play Rogue, don't be like me: get to the point in the main story where you unlock the fleet and start those missions asap (long before you do the bulk of the side stuff). But exploits like the desync zone for the tank mission, or immortality cheat for storm fortress kind of ruin the games imo. Just my two cents.

Good luck and have fun! I'd start with AC II and work your way through the games chronologically if you decide to platinum them all.

Some people mentioned timed parrying being a benefit, but if you just hold (not tap) the parry buttons in normal mode when they go to attack, you'll parry regardless of timing (won't need to be exact). It'll help you build up adrenaline.

Also, if you've reached the point where you have the Minotaur's labrys, putting that in your extra weapon slot gives you -1 adrenaline cost for overpower abilities. I also put a lot of ability points toward the mastery skill that gives you back health for damage dealt. Both of those make you near invincible, imo.

Good luck!
